given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today
given.why: Both loans are due 2026-03-16, the clock is set to 2026-03-17, and the test asserts that both are reminded.

The clock is always set to 10:00Z, so taking today from the local date instead of the UTC date gives the same day in nearly every runner timezone. No test sets the clock near midnight, where the two dates differ.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The test starts from a fresh in-memory database with no reminders and expects both loans to be sent.

then.why: The fake's `sent` list must contain both reminders and have length 2, so a run that never calls the client fails.
Each sent reminder must carry its own loan's memberId (member-1 or member-2).
The test reads the reminders table and expects exactly one row per loan.
`sent_on` must be 2026-03-17, today, not the due date 2026-03-16.
B3: if the code recorded before asking, the refused loan would get a reminders row, and B3's exact `toEqual` on the table would fail.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice on the same day, so loan1 already has today's reminder when the second run starts.
loan2 is past due (due 03-16) and returned before the job runs.
loan3 is due 2026-03-17, the same day as the run, which tests the boundary.

then.why: On an array, `toMatchObject` requires the same length, so a second send for loan1, or any send for loan2 or loan3, fails the test.

given.why: The fake is set to refuse loan1 with the reason "Notifications API answered 503".
B5: the client's test shows a failed connection comes back as `refused`, which is the same outcome this service test covers.

then.why: The reminders table must equal exactly loan2's row.
The log check is an exact `toContainEqual` on the event name.
The level must be `warn`.
The fields must have `loanId` equal to loan1, and the match is exact.
`error` must be the reason the fake returned, word for word.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: loan1 is due first (03-15), so it is refused before loan2 is handled, and loan2 must still be sent and recorded.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: The test checks the last log entry after a full run over three overdue loans.

then.why: The event name must equal `reminders.finished` exactly.
The level must equal `info`.
`sent` must be 2.

The test sets up one refusal, but `expect.objectContaining({ sent: 2 })` never looks at `failed`, so the code could drop or miscount it and pass. mutants.json lists a `failed` mutant for this row, but this assertion can't kill it.

given.why: Every B5 test calls the real client with a reminder.

then.why: The recorded method must equal POST.
The path must be /notifications. The host is pinned too, because the handler matches only NOTIFICATIONS_PATH and unhandled requests are errors (tests/support/http-interceptor.setup.ts:4).
The content-type must be application/json, and the body is parsed as JSON.
The body is compared with `toEqual`, so the memberId key and value are both pinned.
The body is compared exactly.
The body is compared exactly, including the nested data keys.
Answers of 200, 202 and 204 must each come back as `accepted`, so a check for 200 only fails.
A 400 must come back as `refused`, so treating only 5xx as refused fails. No test sends a 3xx or a 5xx.

then.part: or a failed connection as refused
then.why: `HttpResponse.error()` must come back as `refused` and must not throw.

then.part: with a reason naming the status
then.why: The reason must contain "400".

then.part: or saying the API was unreachable
then.why: The reason must contain "unreachable".
